notes: SHIP v1.14.449 - R8 FINAL POLISH, AND THE PROGRAMME MEASURED END TO END. R8 WAS MOSTLY ALREADY CLOSED, AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. Its list reads cabinet and material realism, LED restraint, vent and detail density, label clarity, contact shadows, subtle floor reflection, selected-rack emphasis, cyan and violet balance. Six of those eight were already delivered or already ruled: material realism at R4 (powder coat replacing the mirror, plus the light edge that pays for it), LED restraint at R3 (neutral cool white, nothing blinking), cyan and violet balance at R5 (the rig onto the --cyan and --vio tokens), selected-rack emphasis verified intact at R6 (1.0 then 0.55 then 0.32 then 0.30 and 0.22), and BOTH floor items are ruled rather than open - the floor is a MeshBasicMaterial taking NO light, NO env and NO shadow because receiveShadow was REMOVED to kill a sweeping specular pool, and the subtle reflection section 26 asks for is the wet clone that already ships. Adding a contact shadow would revert a documented fix. THE ONE REAL GAP WAS DETAIL AND LABEL CLARITY, and it was a sampler setting. The rail perforation - three EIA-310 square holes per U, tiled once per U across totalU on four rails - is the finest repeating detail on the cabinet and is read at a grazing angle in every ISO view. It set magFilter and nothing else, so the mip chain averaged that hole pattern into a grey smear exactly where section 35 says detail must not blur. Anisotropic sampling fixes it without adding one triangle, which is the cheapest tool section 19 permits. The aisle had already set this precedent on its own label textures - engraved type stays sharp at walk angles - so this follows house practice rather than inventing it. Capped at 4, matching the floor texture on the same renderer, because that is where the visible return flattens while bandwidth keeps climbing on mobile. THE PROGRAMME, MEASURED LIKE FOR LIKE. The R1 baseline used a five-device seed and the final gallery uses the nineteen-device s4:099, so those numbers are NOT comparable and were not compared. Instead the pre-programme build v1.14.441 was checked out and run against the IDENTICAL nineteen-device seed. Build preview, before then after: objects 1715 to 1521, meshes 1610 to 1416, geometries 1547 to 1353, materials 351 to 306, triangles 57200 to 51542, draw calls 484 to 417, renderers live 1 to 1, pixel ratio 2 to 2. Forge aisle: objects 1843 to 1649, materials 401 to 356, triangles 58000 to 52342, draw calls 73 to 73. EVERY COUNT WENT DOWN. The rack looks substantially better and costs about 14 percent fewer draw calls and 10 percent fewer triangles than it did before the programme started - the instanced switch LEDs from R3 and the chassis material cache from R4 more than paid for the deeper cabinet. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec ALONE): 33 = 4, 32 = 3, 31 = 4, 30 = 4, 20 = 6, 02-build-forge = 14 including the x10 aisle round trip, 08-forge-layout = 17 passed with 1 skipped. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, 12 style blocks brace-balanced, 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep at .449. DEVICE-VERIFY: open BUILD with an active rack and switch FRONT to ISO. PASS is the mounting-hole pattern staying crisp on the rails at the ISO angle instead of smearing to grey. FAIL is rails that look softer than before, or any change to tray colours or rack brightness.
